findings.reason: a node dispatched with s19 as written would violate a recorded lead decision and land a graph population the plan explicitly defers, so the plan's own instruction to the worker is wrong until one of the two statements changes.
findings.text: s19's Delivers makes every one of the feed's 2,898 catalogue-present variables a facility signal in the graph now, while s12 states "Only the pilot set already written to the graph stays there; the remaining variables enter the graph later, through the discovery pipeline's own command" (plan.html:108) — the two sections cannot both hold: a worker on s19 writes ~2,898 signals that s12's decision (version 43) says must not be in the graph yet, and a worker on s12's rule has no mandate to accept them. The plan must either revise the pilot-set restriction and say so in s12 (or in a decision), or have s19 route these variables through the pipeline path s12 names, and the section's dependency set will change accordingly

findings.reason: the node would otherwise close on a control that any implementation, including one that indexes the name-only description, passes.
findings.text: the negative control reads "a signal whose feed description is only its own name is not returned by a search for a described quantity on the strength of that text" but names no query, so a run can pick any described quantity that the signal never matched and the control passes whatever the indexing code does; "on the strength of that text" cannot be attributed when the query is unconstrained, so the check cannot show the guard (a name-only description not offered to search) fires. It becomes falsifiable only against a stated query, e.g. the description text itself or a pre-registered query whose expected signal is the name-only one

findings.reason: the endpoint is unreachable as written, so the plan needs a declared schema change (or a named existing slot) before a node can implement it without guessing.
findings.text: the endpoint requires each signal to be "marked with the feed as their source and the feed's own update time", but `FacilitySignal` in imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:2819-3390 carries `description`, `source_description`, `unit`, `discovery_source` and `discovered_at` and no slot for a feed identity or the feed's own update time; `archive_metadata` is the archive's document, not the feed's, so the record the section says it delivers is not representable without a schema change, and s19 (unlike s16) declares none. A worker must either invent a slot, a plan-level schema decision the section leaves to them, or drop the feed's update time and close on a record that does not match the Delivers text
